intent: One hospital room in Paris: the old method wiped off the screen, the paper tube, the Greek name and the book, then the irony of the doctor's own death.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where was the stethoscope INVENTED?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: France. In 1816, at the Necker Hospital in Paris, René Laennec rolled a sheet of paper into a tube.

lines.direction: tighten on Paris; an EAR TO CHEST plate waits at the bottom; an ear sticker on 'ear'; a blushing face on 'awkward'; on 'heartbeat' the plate wipes away and a heart sticker pulses; the French flag-ball grins
lines.text: Doctors pressed an ear to the chest. With a young woman patient Laennec found that awkward; the tube carried her heartbeat clearly.

lines.direction: ease back over France; the CHEST / LOOK split of Greek roots on 'Greek'; a book sticker on 'published' with the 1819 card; the Paris pin leaves at the end
lines.text: He named it the stethoscope, from the Greek for chest and look, and published his findings in 1819.

lines.direction: drift west to Brittany; the Quimper pin and tag on 'died'; a lungs sticker on 'tuberculosis'; the British flag-ball thinks; France pulses on 'best'
lines.text: Laennec died at 45 of tuberculosis, the disease his own instrument diagnosed best.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
